name: London, UK 🇬🇧
subtitle: From St. JOHN to Dishoom — London's greatest tables
items: St. JOHN (Smithfield, Fergus Henderson — nose-to-tail, changed how Britain eats, since 1994)
Dishoom (multiple, Bombay café — the bacon naan roll changed morning London)
The River Café (Hammersmith, Ruth Rogers — Italian, outdoor terrace, the River Thames)
Barrafina (multiple, Spanish tapas — no reservations, worth every minute in queue)
Gymkhana (Mayfair, Indian fine dining — 1 Michelin star, game seekh kebab)
Kiln (Soho, Thai grill — coal-fired, natural wine, the Soho queue is real)
The Clove Club (Shoreditch, Isaac McHale — 1-star, seasonal British)
Brat (Shoreditch, Tomos Parry — whole turbot on charcoal, 1-star)
Lyle's (Shoreditch, James Lowe — 1-star, daily-changing)
Rules (Covent Garden, since 1798 — the oldest restaurant in London)
J Sheekey (Covent Garden, theatreland seafood since 1896)
Hawksmoor (multiple, best steakhouse in London + phenomenal cocktails)
Flat Iron (multiple, affordable steak — £15-ish, cut from shared joints)
Smoking Goat (Borough, Ben Chapman — Thai BBQ)
Bao (Soho, Taiwanese — gua bao and confit pork rice, queue minimum 45 min)
Ottolenghi (multiple, Yotam Ottolenghi — the deli that changed modern cooking)
Moro (Exmouth Market, Moorish — Sam & Sam Clark, since 1997)
Quo Vadis (Soho, Jeremy Lee — the best lunch in London)
Naughty Piglets (Brixton, natural wine + modern European)
The Wolseley (Piccadilly, grand café — breakfast is the move)
